reasoning: This is a narrative review article synthesizing existing literature on schizophrenia's neurochemistry, circuits, symptoms, and treatments. It does not involve generating or using any specific software tools, nor does it generate or analyze new datasets. It is a conceptual/clinical review rather than an empirical study involving software or data.

This is a clinical consensus guideline paper synthesizing existing literature and expert opinion to produce treatment recommendations. It does not develop or use any software as part of the research process, nor does it generate or use a specific dataset for analysis; instead it reviews systematic reviews and primary literature to form evidence-based recommendations. Thus it falls under No Software, No Data.

The study uses existing software (TopoToolbox V2) to process a nationwide DEM, without substantially developing or extending the tool itself - it's applied as a workflow. However, the research generates a new national-scale geodatabase of catchment characteristics (morphometric and topographic data for 128 catchments), which is a novel dataset shared via an interactive ArcGIS web-application for public access. This constitutes substantial new data generation and sharing, fitting D1, while the software (TopoToolbox) is merely used as an existing tool, fitting S2.

The paper develops a visualization/graph-drawing tool that implements Jaya algorithm and its enhanced (LHS) version, which constitutes newly developed software playing a substantial role in the research (the tool integrates search methods and evaluates layouts). This is S1. For data, the authors generate synthetic graph datasets using the Erdős–Rényi model with varying nodes/edges specifically for benchmarking, which is newly generated data central to the experiments (real-world datasets are also used, but the synthetic data generation is a substantial, research-specific contribution), placing it in D1.

This is a study protocol for a future randomised clinical trial. No data has been collected or analysed yet, and no software is developed or used as part of the research described (only mention of online questionnaires, which is administrative/incidental). Since it is a protocol paper describing planned methodology, neither data nor software play a substantial role in the current paper's research goals.

This is a workforce/education survey study that generated new primary data through literature review, semi-structured interviews with lead nurses/stakeholders, and surveys of four cohorts of nurses/midwives (n=153) over 2019-22, plus thematic analysis of qualitative responses. This new empirical data (survey scores, interview findings, competency framework) was collected/generated by the research team as a core part of the study. No specialized software tools are described as being developed or substantially used to achieve the research goals; standard statistical analysis (e.g., Likert scale scoring) would be incidental, not a research focus. Hence classified as No Software, Data Generated (S3D1).

The paper is an editorial/introduction to a special issue on machine learning and deep learning applications in finance, education, and healthcare. Based on the title and journal type, this appears to be an editorial overview piece summarizing contributions rather than presenting original software or data. No specific software tools or datasets are described as generated or substantially used within this paper itself.

The study uses existing/standard radiotherapy planning and TCP modeling tools (not a novel software developed by the authors), so no new software is generated or shared - this is S3 (No Software) since software (e.g., treatment planning system, TCP modeling) is used routinely but is not a research contribution itself. On the data side, the authors collected pre-treatment DW-MRI/ADC data from ten GBM patients and derived new cellular density maps, TCP maps, and dose escalation plans specifically for this research - this constitutes newly generated patient-derived imaging and computational data central to achieving the research goals, corresponding to D1 (Data Generated).

The study generates new data by applying a multiplexed immunofluorescence workflow to patient tissue samples (NLPHL and THRLBCL cases), producing novel immune cell phenotype data that is central to the research goals (D1). This involves using existing multiplex immunofluorescence imaging/analysis software and platforms to quantify immune cell markers, but there is no indication the research team developed new software tools or substantially extended existing software as part of this study (S2).

The study collected new survey data (BRCS, MBI-GS, custom Covid-19 stress questionnaire) from 384 startup directors/representatives, which constitutes newly generated data central to the research goals. The GMDH neural network methodology used is an existing established technique (group method of data handling), not a novel software tool developed by the authors; there's no mention of releasing new software or substantially extending existing neural network software - they applied an existing method/algorithm to their data. Hence software is used (existing method) while data is generated (new survey data collected specifically for this study).

The study generates new experimental data (a novel crystal structure of AMG-176 bound to Mcl-1, plus NMR conformer analysis data) that is central to the research goals and presumably deposited (e.g., PDB), fitting D1. For software, the authors likely used standard existing crystallography/NMR data processing and structure refinement software (e.g., PHENIX, CCP4, NMR analysis tools) without developing new software themselves, fitting S2.

This is a cluster randomized controlled trial that generated new primary data through repeated assessments of mothers and children (pregnancy, 3, 6, 15, 24 months) across 8 clinics - this data collection is central to the research goal and represents newly generated data. There is no mention of any software tool being developed or used substantially (e.g., no custom analysis software, apps, or platforms described as playing a substantial role); standard statistical analysis is implied but not highlighted as a research contribution. Thus this fits No Software (S3) and Data Generated (D1).

The researchers developed new harmonised symptom/blood test phenotypes (coded lists in Read v2/CTV3) which constitute a substantial data resource generated as part of the study and intended to be useful for other researchers - this represents newly generated data (the phenotype code lists) that plays a substantial role and is shared. They analyzed existing EHR data (UK Biobank and CPRD linked to cancer registry) but the phenotype codelists themselves are a novel data product of the research, justifying D1. No new software tools were developed or shared; statistical analysis used standard Poisson regression models via standard statistical software, not a substantial custom software contribution, so S3 applies.

This is a perspective/opinion piece discussing decolonisation of the psychology curriculum. It does not involve any software development or use, nor does it generate or use any empirical data—it's a conceptual/argumentative essay drawing on existing literature and discourse without data analysis or software tools.

The paper's core contribution is the compilation and publication of a new global dataset (DOCU-CLIM) of 621 documentary climate time series, gathered and harmonized by the research team from historical documents. This is clearly Data Generated (D1) as it is a novel, shared dataset that is itself a primary research output. The paper describes evaluation via proxy forward models but does not mention developing or substantially extending any software tool as part of the research - standard statistical/correlation analyses are used without indication of new software being created or a specific existing software package being central to the methodology. Thus, software does not play a substantial role (S3)."

The study generated new sediment core metabarcoding data spanning 100 years (DNA sequences, biocide measurements, climate correlations) - this is newly generated data (D1). They also developed a conceptual/computational framework using explainable network models with multimodal learning specifically designed for this biodiversity-environment analysis, which constitutes new software/methodology developed as part of the research (S1), going beyond simply using existing off-the-shelf tools.

This is a narrative/state-of-the-art review article summarizing existing literature on BBB imaging techniques and their clinical relevance. It does not report generation or use of any specific software tool, nor does it generate or analyze a specific dataset. It synthesizes findings from prior studies without creating new data or software.

This study collected new primary survey data from 10,007 respondents in Malang, Indonesia, through a cross-sectional survey specifically designed for this research - this constitutes newly generated data central to the research goals. The analysis was conducted using standard statistical techniques (linear regression, logistic regression, generalized structural equation modeling) via standard statistical software (e.g., Stata, SPSS, or similar), which is not custom-developed nor a focus of the research; no new software tool was created or shared. Therefore, software does not play a substantial, novel role (S3), while data collection and generation is central and substantial (D1).

This is a review article discussing concepts, challenges, and computational tools relevant to post-GWAS interpretation of AD and PD risk alleles in microglia. It does not generate or substantially use specific software or datasets itself; it synthesizes existing literature and discusses methodologies/tools conceptually without performing new analyses or presenting original data.

This is a narrative review article summarizing existing literature on MAIT cells and the microbiome. It does not report generation or use of any specific software tools, nor does it generate or analyze new datasets. No computational methods or data analysis are described; it is purely a synthesis of published findings.

The researchers developed a novel counterfactual GAN architecture specifically for this study, representing new software that plays a central role in generating synthetic OCT images and longitudinal time series - this is a substantial software contribution (S1). For data, they used an existing large-scale dataset (85,709 adults' OCT images from the UK Biobank population study), which is pre-existing data used for training/analysis rather than newly generated by the research team (D2).

The researchers used an existing pretrained language model (GPT-2) and existing NLP embedding methods (software tools) to generate simulations rather than developing new software themselves—though they provide a Python tutorial, this is more of a demonstration/dissemination script rather than substantially new research software. However, they generated new data: the simulated FTD-like narratives produced by perturbing GPT-2's parameters (stochasticity, memory span) constitute newly generated data central to the research goals, which they use to validate their approach and presumably share via the tutorial/paper materials. Thus: Software Used (S2) since GPT-2 and standard NLP metrics are existing tools not substantially extended, and Data Generated (D1) since the simulated narratives are new data central to the study.

This is a study protocol for a cross-sectional survey that will generate new primary data (survey responses on SSI prevention practices) collected specifically for this research and reported as a key output. The survey is administered using an existing commercial platform, Qualtrics XM, which is used but not developed by the research team, making the software aspect S2. Since new data will be generated (though not yet, this is a protocol paper describing planned data collection), it falls under D1.

This is a clinical pharmacology study (phase 1 crossover trials) generating new pharmacokinetic data (Cmax, AUC values) from healthy subjects on drug-drug interactions with rezafungin. No new software tools were developed or used substantially - standard statistical analysis was applied. The primary contribution is new clinical trial data on drug interactions, making this D1 (Data Generated) and S3 (No Software) since software plays no substantial role in the research goals.

The study uses existing UK Biobank data (anthropometric, physical activity, dietary, FFQ) to operationalise a pre-existing standardised scoring system; no new dataset is generated/published, and no new software tool is developed or released - standard statistical calculations are performed to derive scores, so software is not a substantial research output. Thus it fits Data Used (existing UK Biobank data) and No Software (no novel software generated or used as a substantial research method).

This is a narrative review article discussing existing cardiovascular risk assessment methods, biomarkers, and ocular imaging concepts. It does not generate or substantially use any specific software tool, nor does it generate or analyze a dataset - it synthesizes and discusses literature without performing new data analysis or software development.

The study uses Google Trends, an existing publicly available data source, to obtain search volume data (existing data, not generated by the researchers) - D2. They likely used existing statistical software (e.g., Joinpoint Regression software from NCI) to perform joinpoint regression analysis, which is an established tool used but not developed by the researchers - S2. No new software or dataset was created/published as part of this research.

This qualitative study generated new primary data through in-depth interviews with dental officers and managers in Fiji, which was thematically analyzed - this constitutes newly generated data central to the research goals. No specialized software was developed or notably used (manual thematic analysis was performed), so software does not play a substantial role, placing it in S3. Since new interview data was collected specifically for this study, it falls under D1.

This is a systematic review and meta-analysis that synthesizes existing published studies and national surveys on adolescent nutrition in Ethiopia. It uses existing data (extracted from 76 articles and 2 national surveys) to compute pooled prevalence estimates via meta-analysis, but does not generate new primary data itself. No new or substantially extended software is developed; standard statistical/meta-analysis tools would be used only in a routine, incidental capacity (not detailed or highlighted as a research contribution), so software does not play a substantial, novel role beyond standard analysis. Thus it falls under No Software (S3) and Data Used (D2).

The study collected new experimental data (HD-sEMG recordings and decomposed motor unit firing data) from 18 children, which constitutes newly generated data specific to this research (D1). For analysis, they used existing decomposition software/algorithms for extracting motor unit action potentials from EMG signals, which is standard existing software (e.g., decomposition algorithms) rather than software newly developed by the authors as a research contribution, placing it under S2 (Software Used).
